fr: Le livre que je lis en ce moment appartient à ma sœur.
en: The book that I am reading right now belongs to my sister.
ipa: /lə livʁ kə ʒə li ɑ̃ sə mɔ.mɑ̃ a.paʁ.tjɛ̃ a ma sœʁ/
notes: Que functions here as a direct object relative pronoun and must not be replaced by qui, which is reserved for the subject position.

fr: C'est la maison dont je t'ai parlé hier soir.
en: This is the house I told you about last night.
ipa: /sɛ la mɛ.zɔ̃ dɔ̃ ʒə tε paʁ.le jɛʁ swaʁ/
notes: Dont replaces de plus a noun and is easy to confuse with d'où; here it marks the object of parler de.

fr: Ces enfants jouent dans le jardin pendant que leurs parents travaillent.
en: These children are playing in the garden while their parents work.
ipa: /se z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ ʒu dɑ̃ lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃ pɑ̃.dɑ̃ kə lœʁ pa.ʁɑ̃ tʁa.vaj/
notes: Ces, the demonstrative plural, sounds identical to ses and c'est, so context alone decides the correct spelling.

fr: Je me demande si tu leur as déjà envoyé le message.
en: I wonder if you already sent them the message.
ipa: /ʒə mə də.mɑ̃d si ty lœʁ a de.ʒa ɑ̃.vwa.je lə me.saʒ/
notes: Leur as an indirect object pronoun never takes an s here, unlike the possessive adjective leurs.

fr: Nous nous sommes levés très tôt pour attraper le train.
en: We got up very early to catch the train.
ipa: /nu nu sɔm lə.ve tʁɛ to puʁ a.tʁa.pe lə tʁɛ̃/
notes: The reflexive pronoun nous is repeated before the verb, and the past participle levés agrees in gender and number with the subject.

fr: Elle a acheté cette robe parce qu'elle lui allait parfaitement.
en: She bought that dress because it suited her perfectly.
ipa: /ɛl a a.ʃə.te sɛt ʁɔb paʁ.skɛl lɥi a.lɛ paʁ.fɛt.mɑ̃/
notes: Lui here is an indirect object pronoun meaning to her, and elle elides to qu'elle before the vowel of the conjunction.

fr: Le professeur dont les cours sont si populaires part à la retraite.
en: The teacher whose classes are so popular is retiring.
ipa: /lə pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ dɔ̃ le kuʁ sɔ̃ si pɔ.py.lɛʁ paʁ a la ʁə.tʁɛt/
notes: Dont expresses possession here, replacing de ce professeur, and should never be written as two words d'ont.

fr: Où as-tu rangé les clés que je cherche depuis ce matin?
en: Where did you put the keys that I have been looking for since this morning?
ipa: /u a ty ʁɑ̃.ʒe le kle kə ʒə ʃɛʁʃ də.pɥi sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: Où as a question word carries a grave accent and is often mixed up with the conjunction ou, which never takes one.

fr: Ses collègues lui ont offert un cadeau pour son anniversaire.
en: Her colleagues gave her a gift for her birthday.
ipa: /se kɔ.lɛg lɥi ɔ̃ ɔ.fɛʁ œ̃ ka.do puʁ sɔ.n‿a.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ/
notes: Ses, the plural possessive, sounds exactly like ces and c'est, so only meaning can tell them apart.

fr: Je crois que ce restaurant dont on parle tant vaut vraiment le détour.
en: I think that restaurant everyone talks about is really worth the detour.
ipa: /ʒə kʁwa kə sə ʁɛs.to.ʁɑ̃ dɔ̃ ɔ̃ paʁl tɑ̃ vo vʁɛ.mɑ̃ lə de.tuʁ/
notes: The impersonal pronoun on triggers a third person singular verb even though it can mean we in spoken French.

fr: Il faut que nous y allions avant que le magasin ne ferme.
en: We need to go there before the store closes.
ipa: /il fo kə nu z‿i a.ljɔ̃ a.vɑ̃ kə lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ nə fɛʁm/
notes: The subjunctive ending of allions keeps a silent group of letters that is often dropped in dictation, and y stands for the place already mentioned.

fr: Cette lettre, je l'ai écrite hier soir avant de me coucher.
en: That letter, I wrote it last night before going to bed.
ipa: /sɛt lɛtʁ ʒə lε e.kʁit jɛʁ swaʁ a.vɑ̃ də mə ku.ʃe/
notes: Because the direct object lettre comes before the verb through l', the past participle écrite agrees in the feminine.

fr: Les enfants dont je m'occupe adorent les histoires que je leur raconte.
en: The children I take care of love the stories I tell them.
ipa: /le z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ dɔ̃ ʒə mɔ.kyp a.dɔʁ le z‿is.twaʁ kə ʒə lœʁ ʁa.kɔ̃t/
notes: Dont replaces de followed by a noun, here for s'occuper de, while leur stays invariable as an indirect object.

fr: Je pense qu'il faut absolument que tu lui écrives avant vendredi.
en: I think you absolutely need to write to her before Friday.
ipa: /ʒə pɑ̃s kil fo ap.sɔ.ly.mɑ̃ kə ty lɥi e.kʁiv a.vɑ̃ vɑ̃.dʁə.di/
notes: The subjunctive form écrives ends in a silent s that is easy to forget after the pronoun tu.

fr: Ce sont ces photos que ta mère voulait absolument te montrer.
en: These are the photos your mother absolutely wanted to show you.
ipa: /sə sɔ̃ se fɔ.to kə ta mɛʁ vu.lɛ ap.sɔ.ly.mɑ̃ tə mɔ̃.tʁe/
notes: Ce sont introduces the plural, while ces marks the demonstrative photos, both sounding like se and ses.

fr: Elle se demande pourquoi il ne lui a jamais répondu.
en: She wonders why he never answered her.
ipa: /ɛl sə də.mɑ̃d puʁ.kwa il nə lɥi a ʒa.mɛ ʁe.pɔ̃.dy/
notes: Se, the reflexive pronoun, is a common homophone trap with ce, the demonstrative pronoun.

fr: Nous avons visité le village où mes grands-parents se sont rencontrés.
en: We visited the village where my grandparents met.
ipa: /nu z‿a.vɔ̃ vi.zi.te lə vi.laʒ u me gʁɑ̃.pa.ʁɑ̃ sə sɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃.tʁe/
notes: Où indicates place and takes a grave accent, unlike the conjunction ou meaning or.

fr: C'est un projet auquel je tiens énormément depuis le début.
en: This is a project that I have cared about enormously from the start.
ipa: /sɛ.t‿œ̃ pʁɔ.ʒɛ o.kɛl ʒə tjɛ̃ e.nɔʁ.me.mɑ̃ də.pɥi lə de.by/
notes: Auquel contracts à and lequel and must agree with the masculine noun projet.

fr: Je leur ai promis que je les appellerais dès mon arrivée.
en: I promised them that I would call them as soon as I arrived.
ipa: /ʒə lœʁ ε pʁɔ.mi kə ʒə le z‿a.pɛl.ʁɛ dɛ mɔ.n‿a.ʁi.ve/
notes: Leur stays invariable as an indirect object while les, the direct object, triggers the liaison before appellerais.

fr: Voici la clé que tu cherchais partout depuis ce matin.
en: Here is the key that you were looking for everywhere since this morning.
ipa: /vwa.si la kle kə ty ʃɛʁ.ʃɛ paʁ.tu də.pɥi sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: Que introduces the relative clause as a direct object and should not be replaced by qui, which is reserved for subjects.

fr: Il y a plusieurs raisons pour lesquelles je n'ai pas pu venir.
en: There are several reasons why I could not come.
ipa: /il i a ply.zjœʁ ʁɛ.zɔ̃ puʁ lɛs.kɛl ʒə nε pa py və.niʁ/
notes: Lesquelles must agree in gender and number with raisons, a common source of accord mistakes.

fr: Ma sœur, dont le mari est médecin, habite à Lyon depuis dix ans.
en: My sister, whose husband is a doctor, has lived in Lyon for ten years.
ipa: /ma sœʁ dɔ̃ lə ma.ʁi ɛ med.sɛ̃ a.bit a ljɔ̃ də.pɥi di z‿ɑ̃/
notes: Dont expresses possession within the relative clause, replacing de son mari.

fr: Je n'y crois plus, même si tout le monde continue d'y penser.
en: I no longer believe it, even though everyone keeps thinking about it.
ipa: /ʒə ni kʁwa ply mɛm si tu lə mɔ̃d kɔ̃.ti.ny di pɑ̃.se/
notes: The pronoun y replaces à cela and elides its own vowel before continue, a step easy to skip by mistake.

fr: Ce livre, je te le prête volontiers, mais rends-le-moi vite.
en: This book, I gladly lend it to you, but give it back to me quickly.
ipa: /sə livʁ ʒə tə lə pʁɛt vɔ.lɔ̃.tje mɛ ʁɑ̃d lə mwa vit/
notes: In the imperative, the pronouns le and moi attach after the verb with hyphens instead of coming before it.

fr: Les valises que nous avons préparées hier sont déjà dans la voiture.
en: The suitcases we packed yesterday are already in the car.
ipa: /le va.liz kə nu z‿a.vɔ̃ pʁe.pa.ʁe jɛʁ sɔ̃ de.ʒa dɑ̃ la vwa.tyʁ/
notes: The past participle préparées agrees with the feminine plural direct object valises placed before the verb.

fr: C'est toi qui as raison, pas moi, alors arrête de me contredire.
en: You are the one who is right, not me, so stop contradicting me.
ipa: /sɛ twa ki a ʁɛ.zɔ̃ pa mwa a.lɔʁ a.ʁɛt də mə kɔ̃.tʁə.diʁ/
notes: Qui as the subject relative pronoun keeps the verb in the second person here, agreeing with toi.

fr: Nous en avons déjà discuté plusieurs fois sans jamais trouver de solution.
en: We have already discussed it several times without ever finding a solution.
ipa: /nu z‿ɑ̃ n‿a.vɔ̃ de.ʒa dis.ky.te ply.zjœʁ fwa sɑ̃ ʒa.mɛ tʁu.ve də sɔ.ly.sjɔ̃/
notes: En replaces de cela and creates a nasal liaison sound between nous and avons that is easy to miss in dictation.

fr: Le quartier où j'ai grandi a beaucoup changé ces dernières années.
en: The neighborhood where I grew up has changed a lot in recent years.
ipa: /lə kaʁ.tje u ʒε gʁɑ̃.di a bo.ku ʃɑ̃.ʒe se dɛʁ.njɛʁ a.ne/
notes: Où marks the place in this relative clause, distinct from the conjunction ou that never carries an accent.

fr: Elle m'a rendu le livre qu'elle m'avait emprunté le mois dernier.
en: She returned the book she had borrowed from me last month.
ipa: /ɛl ma ʁɑ̃.dy lə livʁ kɛl ma.vɛ.t‿ɑ̃.pʁœ̃.te lə mwa dɛʁ.nje/
notes: Qu'elle results from the elision of que before a vowel and should never be spelled quelle in this context.

fr: Ce sont mes cousins qui nous ont invités au mariage la semaine dernière.
en: It is my cousins who invited us to the wedding last week.
ipa: /sə sɔ̃ me ku.zɛ̃ ki nu z‿ɔ̃.t‿ɛ̃.vi.te o ma.ʁjaʒ la sə.mɛn dɛʁ.njɛʁ/
notes: Qui as subject keeps the past participle invités agreeing with the plural subject cousins, not with nous.

fr: Je voudrais savoir ce que tu penses vraiment de cette idée.
en: I would like to know what you really think of this idea.
ipa: /ʒə vu.dʁɛ sa.vwaʁ sə kə ty pɑ̃s vʁɛ.mɑ̃ də sɛt i.de/
notes: Ce que combines the neutral demonstrative ce with the relative que to mean what, never written se que.

fr: Les amis chez qui nous avons dormi habitent près de la gare.
en: The friends we stayed with live near the station.
ipa: /le z‿a.mi ʃe ki nu z‿a.vɔ̃ dɔʁ.mi a.bit pʁɛ də la gaʁ/
notes: Qui after the preposition chez refers to people, unlike que which introduces a direct object.

fr: Il faut que je lui parle avant qu'elle ne prenne une décision.
en: I need to talk to her before she makes a decision.
ipa: /il fo kə ʒə lɥi paʁl a.vɑ̃ kɛl nə pʁɛn yn de.si.zjɔ̃/
notes: The subjunctive prenne drops the usual d of prendre and ends in a silent e that must still be written.

fr: Cette décision, ce n'est pas moi qui l'ai prise, c'est mon associé.
en: This decision, it was not me who made it, it was my partner.
ipa: /sɛt de.si.zjɔ̃ sə nε pa mwa ki lε pʁiz sɛ mɔ.n‿a.sɔ.sje/
notes: Because the feminine direct object décision precedes the verb through l', the participle prise takes an extra e.

fr: Je me souviens très bien du jour où nous nous sommes rencontrés.
en: I remember very well the day we met.
ipa: /ʒə mə su.vjɛ̃ tʁɛ bjɛ̃ dy ʒuʁ u nu nu sɔm ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃.tʁe/
notes: Où here refers to a moment in time rather than a place, still spelled with the grave accent.

fr: Mes parents, à qui j'ai téléphoné ce matin, arrivent demain soir.
en: My parents, whom I called this morning, arrive tomorrow evening.
ipa: /me pa.ʁɑ̃ a ki ʒε te.le.fɔ.ne sə ma.tɛ̃ a.ʁiv də.mɛ̃ swaʁ/
notes: À qui replaces téléphoner à mes parents, since téléphoner takes an indirect object introduced by à.

fr: Ce ne sont pas les résultats que nous espérions obtenir cette année.
en: These are not the results that we hoped to get this year.
ipa: /sə nə sɔ̃ pa le ʁe.zyl.ta kə nu z‿ɛs.pe.ʁjɔ̃ ɔp.tə.niʁ sɛt a.ne/
notes: Ce ne sont pas keeps ce as the subject pronoun, distinct from the possessive ses that sounds the same.

fr: Elle a fini par accepter le poste qu'on lui proposait depuis des mois.
en: She finally accepted the position that had been offered to her for months.
ipa: /ɛl a fi.ni paʁ ak.sɛp.te lə pɔst kɔ̃ lɥi pʁɔ.pɔ.zɛ də.pɥi de mwa/
notes: Lui replaces à elle as an indirect object and never adds an s regardless of number.

fr: Nous te remercions pour tout ce que tu as fait pour nous cette année.
en: We thank you for everything you did for us this year.
ipa: /nu tə ʁə.mɛʁ.sjɔ̃ puʁ tu sə kə ty a fɛ puʁ nu sɛt a.ne/
notes: Tout ce que combines the invariable ce with que, and should not be confused with tout ceux que.

fr: C'est le genre de film dont on se souvient longtemps après l'avoir vu.
en: It is the kind of film that you remember for a long time after seeing it.
ipa: /sɛ lə ʒɑ̃ʁ də film dɔ̃ ɔ̃ sə su.vjɛ̃ lɔ̃.tɑ̃ a.pʁɛ la.vwaʁ vy/
notes: Dont replaces de ce film for the verb se souvenir de, and should never be split into d'ont.

fr: Je crois que ces documents sont ceux que le directeur attendait.
en: I think these documents are the ones the director was waiting for.
ipa: /ʒə kʁwa kə se dɔ.ky.mɑ̃ sɔ̃ sø kə lə di.ʁɛk.tœʁ a.tɑ̃.dɛ/
notes: Ces marks the demonstrative plural adjective, while ceux is the pronoun standing for les documents.

fr: Vous leur avez sûrement déjà expliqué pourquoi vous partez si tôt.
en: You have surely already explained to them why you are leaving so early.
ipa: /vu lœʁ a.ve syʁ.mɑ̃ de.ʒa ɛk.spli.ke puʁ.kwa vu paʁ.te si to/
notes: Leur stays invariable here as an indirect object pronoun placed before the auxiliary avez.

fr: Le collègue avec qui je travaille le plus est aussi mon meilleur ami.
en: The colleague I work with the most is also my best friend.
ipa: /lə kɔ.lɛg a.vɛk ki ʒə tʁa.vaj lə plys ε.t‿o.si mɔ̃ mɛ.jœʁ a.mi/
notes: Qui after a preposition like avec refers back to a person, here le collègue.

fr: Elle s'est enfin décidée à leur dire ce qu'elle pensait vraiment.
en: She finally decided to tell them what she really thought.
ipa: /ɛl sɛ.t‿ɑ̃.fɛ̃ de.si.de a lœʁ diʁ sə kɛl pɑ̃.sɛ vʁɛ.mɑ̃/
notes: The reflexive s'est agrees with the feminine subject elle, giving décidée the extra e.

fr: Ce sont ses affaires que j'ai retrouvées sous le lit ce matin.
en: These are her belongings that I found under the bed this morning.
ipa: /sə sɔ̃ se z‿a.fɛʁ kə ʒε ʁə.tʁu.ve su lə li sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: Ses, the possessive, is one more homophone of ces and c'est that dictation often confuses.

fr: Nous y sommes allés ensemble l'été dernier pour la première fois.
en: We went there together last summer for the first time.
ipa: /nu z‿i sɔm.z‿a.le ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl le.te dɛʁ.nje puʁ la pʁə.mjɛʁ fwa/
notes: The pronoun y triggers a liaison with sommes that is easy to miss when writing quickly.

fr: Le film que nous avons vu hier soir m'a beaucoup plu.
en: The film we watched last night pleased me a lot.
ipa: /lə film kə nu z‿a.vɔ̃ vy jɛʁ swaʁ ma bo.ku ply/
notes: Plu, the past participle of plaire, stays invariable even though the direct object precedes the verb.

fr: C'est un secret que je ne peux révéler à personne, pas même à toi.
en: It is a secret that I cannot reveal to anyone, not even to you.
ipa: /sɛ.t‿œ̃ sə.kʁɛ kə ʒə nə pø ʁe.ve.le a pɛʁ.sɔn pa mɛm a twa/
notes: Que introduces the relative clause as the direct object of révéler and must not be replaced by qui.

fr: Ses amis lui ont conseillé de changer complètement de métier.
en: Her friends advised her to change careers completely.
ipa: /se z‿a.mi lɥi ɔ̃ kɔ̃.sɛ.je də ʃɑ̃.ʒe kɔ̃.plɛt.mɑ̃ də me.tje/
notes: Ses marks the possessive plural before amis, triggering a liaison that helps distinguish it from se.

fr: Je ne sais pas ce dont tu as vraiment besoin en ce moment.
en: I do not know what you really need right now.
ipa: /ʒə nə sɛ pa sə dɔ̃ ty a vʁɛ.mɑ̃ bə.zwɛ̃ ɑ̃ sə mɔ.mɑ̃/
notes: Ce dont combines ce with dont for avoir besoin de, a construction often misspelled as ce donc.

fr: C'est la seule personne en qui j'ai encore confiance aujourd'hui.
en: She is the only person I still trust today.
ipa: /sɛ la sœl pɛʁ.sɔn ɑ̃ ki ʒε ɑ̃.kɔʁ kɔ̃.fjɑ̃s o.ʒuʁ.dɥi/
notes: En qui replaces avoir confiance en cette personne, keeping qui for a human antecedent.

fr: Les clients dont nous nous occupons aujourd'hui sont particulièrement exigeants.
en: The clients we are taking care of today are particularly demanding.
ipa: /le kli.jɑ̃ dɔ̃ nu nu z‿ɔ.ky.pɔ̃ o.ʒuʁ.dɥi sɔ̃ paʁ.ti.ky.ljɛʁ.mɑ̃ ɛg.zi.ʒɑ̃/
notes: Dont here replaces de nos clients for the verb s'occuper de, not to be confused with donc.

fr: Elle leur a expliqué que ce n'était pas de sa faute.
en: She explained to them that it was not her fault.
ipa: /ɛl lœʁ a ɛk.spli.ke kə sə nε.tɛ pa də sa fot/
notes: Ce here is the neutral subject pronoun meaning it, never spelled se in this position.

fr: Il faut absolument que tu finisses ce rapport avant ce soir.
en: You absolutely must finish this report before tonight.
ipa: /il fo ap.sɔ.ly.mɑ̃ kə ty fi.nis sə ʁa.pɔʁ a.vɑ̃ sə swaʁ/
notes: The subjunctive finisses ends in a silent es that beginners often forget after tu.

fr: C'est grâce à eux que nous avons pu terminer le projet à temps.
en: It is thanks to them that we managed to finish the project on time.
ipa: /sɛ gʁɑs a ø kə nu z‿a.vɔ̃ py tɛʁ.mi.ne lə pʁɔ.ʒɛ a tɑ̃/
notes: Eux, the stressed pronoun, follows the preposition à and must not be replaced by leur in this position.

fr: Le voisin dont le chien aboie toute la nuit vient de déménager.
en: The neighbor whose dog barks all night just moved away.
ipa: /lə vwa.zɛ̃ dɔ̃ lə ʃjɛ̃ a.bwa tut la nɥi vjɛ̃ də de.me.na.ʒe/
notes: Dont expresses possession here, replacing de ce voisin, the classic trap alongside qui and que.

fr: Ce que je préfère dans cette ville, c'est la tranquillité des petites rues.
en: What I prefer in this city is the peacefulness of the small streets.
ipa: /sə kə ʒə pʁe.fɛʁ dɑ̃ sɛt vil sɛ la tʁɑ̃.ki.li.te de pə.tit ʁy/
notes: Ce que begins the sentence as a neutral relative pronoun, never written se que despite the identical sound.

fr: Je les ai vus hier au marché, mais ils ne m'ont pas reconnu.
en: I saw them yesterday at the market, but they did not recognize me.
ipa: /ʒə le z‿ε vy jɛʁ o maʁ.ʃe mɛ il nə mɔ̃ pa ʁə.kɔ.ny/
notes: Because les precedes the verb as a direct object, the past participle vus agrees in the masculine plural.

fr: C'est exactement ce que nous cherchions depuis le début de nos recherches.
en: That is exactly what we had been looking for since the start of our research.
ipa: /sɛ.t‿ɛg.zak.tə.mɑ̃ sə kə nu ʃɛʁ.ʃjɔ̃ də.pɥi lə de.by də no ʁə.ʃɛʁʃ/
notes: The imperfect ending -ions of cherchions is close in sound to the present tense cherchons, so catching the extra syllable is essential to spell it correctly.

fr: Ses collègues, dont plusieurs sont devenus des amis proches, lui manquent beaucoup.
en: Her colleagues, several of whom have become close friends, are missed a lot by her.
ipa: /se kɔ.lɛg dɔ̃ ply.zjœʁ sɔ̃ də.və.ny de z‿a.mi pʁɔʃ lɥi mɑ̃k bo.ku/
notes: Lui here means to her as an indirect object with manquer, a verb whose construction is reversed compared to English.

fr: Nous ne savons pas encore ce que ces changements vont vraiment signifier pour nous.
en: We do not yet know what these changes will really mean for us.
ipa: /nu nə sa.vɔ̃ pa ɑ̃.kɔʁ sə kə se ʃɑ̃ʒ.mɑ̃ vɔ̃ vʁɛ.mɑ̃ si.ɲi.fje puʁ nu/
notes: Ces marks the demonstrative plural before changements, one more case where sound alone cannot distinguish ces from ses.

fr: Cette maison, je l'aurais achetée si j'en avais eu les moyens.
en: This house, I would have bought it if I had had the means.
ipa: /sɛt mɛ.zɔ̃ ʒə lo.ʁɛ a.ʃə.te si ʒɑ̃ n‿a.vɛ y le mwa.jɛ̃/
notes: Because the feminine object maison precedes through l', the past participle achetée takes the extra e even in the conditional perfect.

fr: Les erreurs que j'aurais pu éviter continuent de me hanter.
en: The mistakes that I could have avoided still haunt me.
ipa: /le z‿ɛ.ʁœʁ kə ʒo.ʁɛ py e.vi.te kɔ̃.ti.ny də mə ɑ̃.te/
notes: Éviter stays as an infinitive after pu, so no agreement applies despite the preceding plural object erreurs.

fr: Ta voiture est plus rapide que la mienne, mais la sienne les dépasse toutes deux.
en: Your car is faster than mine, but hers beats them both.
ipa: /ta vwa.tyʁ ɛ ply ʁa.pid kə la mjɛn mɛ la sjɛn le de.pas tut dø/
notes: La mienne and la sienne are possessive pronouns that must agree with the feminine noun voiture, not with the gender of the owner.

fr: Il aurait fallu qu'elle le sache avant que nous partions sans elle.
en: She should have known before we left without her.
ipa: /il o.ʁɛ fa.ly kɛl lə saʃ a.vɑ̃ kə nu paʁ.tjɔ̃ sɑ̃ z‿ɛl/
notes: Qu'elle results from the elision of que before a vowel and should never be confused with quelle, the interrogative adjective.

fr: Les photos dont je me souviens le mieux sont celles qu'il m'avait envoyées.
en: The photos I remember best are the ones he had sent me.
ipa: /le fɔ.to dɔ̃ ʒə mə su.vjɛ̃ lə mjø sɔ̃ sɛl kil ma.vɛ.t‿ɑ̃.vwa.je/
notes: The past participle envoyées agrees with the feminine plural celles standing in for les photos, since que refers back to it before avait.

fr: Ce n'est pas la mienne, c'est la vôtre que j'ai empruntée sans vous demander.
en: It is not mine, it is yours that I borrowed without asking you.
ipa: /sə nε pa la mjɛn sɛ la votʁ kə ʒε ɑ̃.pʁœ̃.te sɑ̃ vu də.mɑ̃.de/
notes: La vôtre keeps its circumflex accent, a subtle homophone trap distinguishing the possessive pronoun from votre, the possessive adjective.

fr: Les décisions qu'elle aurait prises différemment auraient tout changé.
en: The decisions she would have made differently would have changed everything.
ipa: /le de.si.zjɔ̃ kɛl o.ʁɛ pʁiz di.fe.ʁa.mɑ̃ o.ʁɛ tu ʃɑ̃.ʒe/
notes: Prises agrees with the feminine plural décisions because que, its direct object, comes before the conditional perfect verb.

fr: C'est le mien, pas le tien, alors range-le avant que je ne me fâche.
en: It is mine, not yours, so put it away before I get angry.
ipa: /sɛ lə mjɛ̃ pa lə tjɛ̃ a.lɔʁ ʁɑ̃ʒ lə a.vɑ̃ kə ʒə nə mə fɑʃ/
notes: Le mien and le tien are possessive pronouns whose nasal endings must not be confused with the adjectives mon and ton.

fr: Je doute qu'elle ait vraiment lu tous les documents qu'on lui avait envoyés.
en: I doubt she really read all the documents that had been sent to her.
ipa: /ʒə dut kɛl ɛ vʁɛ.mɑ̃ ly tu le dɔ.ky.mɑ̃ kɔ̃ lɥi a.vɛ.t‿ɑ̃.vwa.je/
notes: Envoyés agrees with the masculine plural documents represented by qu' placed before avait, while ait is the subjunctive of avoir.

fr: S'il avait su à quel point cela lui manquerait, il l'aurait gardée précieusement.
en: If he had known how much he would miss it, he would have kept it carefully.
ipa: /sil a.vɛ sy a kɛl pwɛ̃ sə.la lɥi mɑ̃.kə.ʁɛ il lo.ʁɛ gaʁ.de pʁe.sjø.zə.mɑ̃/
notes: Gardée agrees with the feminine object represented by l', a subtler trap since the antecedent is never named directly in the sentence.

fr: Ce dont elle rêvait depuis toujours s'est enfin réalisé grâce à eux.
en: What she had always dreamed of finally came true thanks to them.
ipa: /sə dɔ̃ ɛl ʁɛ.vɛ də.pɥi tu.ʒuʁ sɛ.t‿ɑ̃.fɛ̃ ʁe.a.li.ze gʁɑs a ø/
notes: Ce dont combines the neutral ce with dont for rêver de, and réalisé stays masculine singular since the neutral ce is its subject.
